We need to propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We need to output JSON tree with type mol, children reaction nodes etc. Need to find appropriate templates: likely steps: 1) amide formation between carboxylic acid and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursor: acid (C=O) part: maybe trans-α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic sulfonyl phenyl. The target has amide linking to aniline (anilide). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give acid (C=O) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Reaction type: amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine). So step 1: target -> acid precursor + aniline.

Second step: the unsaturated acid could be formed via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (maybe c2ccc(/C=C/...)?) Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to sulfonyl phenyl: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)...)cc2. The acid part is α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl sulfone. So we can break the C=C double bond formation and decarboxylation? Wait Doebner gives α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So we can retrosynthesize the unsaturated acid to aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)?) plus malonic acid. So step 2: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)?) plus malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Reaction: Doebner modification (forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). So break the C=C and break one C-CO2H bond.

Third step: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (the other phenyl amine). In target, we have NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl (c1ccc...). So we can break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (maybe p-toluenesulfonyl chloride?) Actually the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring with methyl (C). The sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and aniline (the aniline attached to phenyl ring? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl ring (c1ccc...). That phenyl has a methyl substituent (C). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to that phenyl ring (the aniline). So the sulfonamide formation is between that aniline (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride). Wait the nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the aniline) and also to the sulfonyl group. So the sulfonamide formation step would be: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) + p-toluenesulfonyl chloride -> target sulfonamide (with N attached to both phenyls). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The nitrogen attaches to first phenyl (c1...). So sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (first phenyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride). So we need two aromatic amine precursors: p-toluidine and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (or its sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride can be derived from p-toluenesulfonic acid (or from the aromatic sulfonyl chloride). But we can treat as commercially available.

Thus route: Step 3 (last forward) sulfonamide formation: combine p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C)cc2). That yields sulfonamide intermediate: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C)cc2)cc1 (without the unsaturated amide side chain). Then step 2: Doebner modification attaches the unsaturated acid side chain onto the second phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl). Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl via a carbon chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the Doebner step would be to form the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the sulfonyl phenyl. Starting from aldehyde on that phenyl (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid, produce the unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)...)cc2). So step 2: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid.

Step 1: amide coupling between that unsaturated acid (carboxylic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So final route.
